source_credit: Source: European Central Bank · Key ECB interest rates
caption_intro: A four-year view of the ECB deposit facility rate. The rate rose from -0.50% at the start of 2022 to a 4.00% peak, then ended 2025 at 2.00%. This is a historical illustration covering 2022–2025, not a current-rate update.

slides.title:
Four years.
One rate cycle.
slides.subtitle:
The ECB deposit facility rate, 2022–2025.
From negative territory to 4%, then back to 2%.
slides.explanation:
Each step marks a change in the official rate.
The endpoint is 2 percentage points below the peak.
slides.note: Effective dates shown; rates stay in force between changes.
slides.alt_text: Step chart of the ECB deposit facility rate from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2025. It starts at minus 0.50%, reaches 4.00% on 20 September 2023, and ends at 2.00%. The line uses effective dates and remains flat between changes. Source: European Central Bank.

slides.title:
The climb was steeper
than the descent.
slides.subtitle:
Change in the same rate, in percentage points.
Each year-end compared with the previous year-end.
slides.explanation:
The rate rose by 4.5 points across 2022 and 2023.
It fell by 2 points across 2024 and 2025.
slides.note: Percentage points describe rate differences, not percent returns.
slides.alt_text: Horizontal bar chart of annual changes in the ECB deposit facility rate, in percentage points. 2022: plus 2.5; 2023: plus 2.0; 2024: minus 1.0; 2025: minus 1.0. Each change compares year-end with the preceding year-end. Positive bars are solid navy; negative bars are cream with a navy outline. Source: European Central Bank.
